title: Cilbir: Turkish Poached Eggs on Garlic Yogurt
cuisine_note: Cilbir is Istanbul's favorite late breakfast: cool garlic yogurt under just-set poached eggs, a stream of paprika butter, and raw onion sharpened with sumac on the side.

qty.note: Turkish pul biber is traditional; paprika plus chili flakes stands in

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with the grated garlic and a pinch of the salt in the mixing bowl and leave it on the counter - cold yogurt seizes the eggs on contact.
Toss the red onion with the sumac and a pinch of salt in a small dish and let it macerate for 10 minutes while the eggs poach; it loses its raw bite.

Bring 2 inches of water to a bare simmer in the wide saucepan - bubbles shudder, not roll. Slide in the eggs and poach for 4 minutes, until the whites are fully set and the yolks thickened. Eggs are safe at 160°F (71°C); check the thickest white with a thermometer. Use pasteurized eggs for a looser yolk.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: While the eggs poach, melt the butter in the small skillet with the paprika and chili flakes for 1 minute, until it foams and smells nutty - pull it early; burnt paprika turns bitter.
Spread the yogurt on two warm plates, rest the drained eggs on top, and pour the paprika butter over in streams.
Finish with the dill and the sumac onions alongside, and break into it at the table.
